name: Cao Bang
provinceNote: National Assembly Resolution 202/2025/QH15 left Cao Bang unmerged. It is one of 11 provinces that were not rearranged. Merged provinces elsewhere started work on 1 July 2025.
dotReason: Worth a special trip from Hanoi for Ban Gioc and one other road
summary: A mountain province on the northern border, home to the wide Ban Gioc waterfall and limestone valleys. See the falls and the nearby Nguom Ngao cave, visit Pac Bo and the high Phia Oac forest, and eat sour pho and roast duck in town. Allow two or three nights; it suits road-trippers who like big landscapes.
timeNeeded: 2–3 nights for the falls and one other road
fee: Check on arrival. No geopark-wide ticket was on the pages read.
getThere: Bus from Hanoi. About 280 km and about eight hours on Vietnam Tourism; other desks disagree.
bestMonths: October to April for the roads
seoTitle: Cao Bang travel guide — Ban Gioc and one other road
seoDescription: Plan two or three nights for Ban Gioc plus Pac Bo or Phia Oac. Roads are kinder from October to April. The falls carry more water from June to September.
intro: You come for the wide cascade on the Quay Son, limestone around the river, and a morning that is not a turnaround from Hanoi. Ban Gioc sits in Dam Thuy, more than 80 km east of Cao Bang city. Sleep once in the city, or in the valley, so the falls are a morning.

Stay if the border falls and one other road are the trip. Go to Ha Giang if you wanted the limestone loop instead. Pac Bo is about 55 km north on provincial road 203. Phia Oac is a day west, a national park whose summit is 1,935 m. They are not the same afternoon as the falls.

The bus from Hanoi is the way in. Vietnam Tourism puts the city at about 280 km and about eight hours. Other desks print different distances and times, so treat the road clock as check on arrival. The mistake is spending the only daylight in town, or pairing Ban Gioc with Pac Bo because both names fit on one map.
gettingAround: No flight and no train run Hanoi to Cao Bang on the desks read for this page. Day and overnight buses leave My Dinh. An operator yard lists night buses from My Dinh and Gia Lam and gives its own address on National Highway 3. That is an operator page, so confirm the yard on arrival. Hire a car or a motorbike in the city for the geopark roads. A local bus to the falls or to Pac Bo is check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Cao Bang city
stayAreas.summary: Sleep by the Bang River for the night you arrive, and for a Pac Bo or Phia Oac day. City hotels and guesthouses. No hotel brand as a pick.

stayAreas.name: Dam Thuy
stayAreas.summary: Sleep in the Quay Son valley when Ban Gioc is the morning. Homestays and guesthouses. The city is more than 80 km away.

eat: Breakfast in town is phở chua, bánh cuốn, or phở vịt. Vietnam Tourism names phở chua and bánh cuốn. Báo Cao Bằng describes phở chua as a sour bowl, not a hot beef pho, and bánh cuốn in pork-bone broth. A price is Check on arrival.

The eastern road is roast duck, smoked sausage, and Trùng Khánh chestnuts in autumn. Corn wine belongs with a northern meal. Kim Đồng, in Thục Phán, is the walking street where Báo Cao Bằng placed produce stalls for the 2026 National Day holiday. An ordinary-day clock and stall prices are Check on arrival.
interestsBody: The falls, the lit cave, and the pagoda viewpoint are one eastern day. Pac Bo is the northern half day. Phia Oac is the western day, moss forest up to 1,935 m.

Pho chua is the city bowl, and it is not Hanoi pho. The chestnut and the five-colour rice sit on the same highland table. Kim Dong is the walking street. No boutique and no mall were named for a shopping stop.

interestGroups.title: The border falls
interestGroups.summary: The morning you came for: the cascade on the Quay Son, then the pagoda roof over the same valley.
body: Ban Gioc is the wide cascade at the border, in Dam Thuy, more than 80 km east of the city. A bamboo raft toward the foot is the optional ride. Whether you may cross at the Ban Gioc–Detian scenic route is check on arrival. This page does not state a visa rule.

blocks.heading: The cascade
paragraphs: From the end of November to the beginning of April the management board says the water is very low and asks you to come between 10:30 and 15:30. Vietnam Tourism describes a dry-season dam release between 10:30 and 13:00, and fuller water from June to September.

Width is not one number. The timing notice says about 300 m wide and 35 m high. Vietnam Tourism says the main fall is over 30 m. An indexed provincial feature said about 208 m wide and was not reloaded. The gate fee is check on arrival.

blocks.heading: The pagoda viewpoint
paragraphs: Truc Lam Ban Gioc stands on Phia Nhan. Vietnam Tourism calls the walk short and steep. The frame to keep is the roof and the valley. The falls’ low-water window is still 10:30 to 15:30. A fee for the pagoda is check on arrival.

cards.title: Ban Gioc
cards.summary: The cascade, the river, and the limestone, more than 80 km east of the city. Come between 10:30 and 15:30 when the water is low. The fee is check on arrival.

cards.title: Truc Lam Ban Gioc
cards.summary: A short, steep walk to the pagoda on Phia Nhan. The roof sits over the valley. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: The lit cave
interestGroups.summary: The electrically lit walk about 4 km from the falls. The rough Ban Thuon branch is a different visit.
body: Nguom Ngao is in Ban Gun, Dam Thuy. Vietnam Tourism says the system is 2,144 m, with 948 m open to ordinary visitors, about an hour or more for a one-kilometre walk. The geopark says more than 2,000 m and three mouths: Nguom Ngao, Nguom Lom, and Ban Thuon. The Ban Thuon branch, nearly 3 km, opened for a rougher visit with climbing and wading. The fee is check on arrival.

cards.title: Nguom Ngao
cards.summary: About an hour or more for the lit kilometre, on the same day as the falls. Do not budget the long Ban Thuon branch as that hour. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Pac Bo
interestGroups.summary: A half day north of the city for Coc Bo and the stream, not an add-on to the falls.
body: The relic monograph places Pac Bo at Truong Ha, Ha Quang, about 55 km north on provincial road 203, at km 0 of the Ho Chi Minh Road. The special-national listing is dated 10 May 2012. You walk Coc Bo, where Ho Chi Minh stayed after returning in 1941, and the Lenin stream. The gate fee and the on-site minutes are check on arrival.

cards.title: Pac Bo
cards.summary: About 55 km north on provincial road 203. Coc Bo and the stream are the walk. A special national relic since 10 May 2012. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Phia Oac
interestGroups.summary: A day west of the city for moss forest and the ridge, not for another waterfall.
body: Phia Oac–Phia Den National Park was set by decision 45/QĐ-TTg of 8 January 2014, on 11,960 ha, including moss forest and elfin forest. The summit is 1,935 m. The drive from the city is check on arrival for minutes. The gate fee is check on arrival. A gibbon in the geopark’s forests is not a promise of a sighting on this road.

blocks.heading: The moss forest
paragraphs: The road climbs from evergreen forest into moss and elfin forest as the air cools. Give it a clear day. Storms on the mountain road are check on arrival.

blocks.heading: The ridge
paragraphs: The western route also names the hanging valley, the Red Villa, and Kolia tea. Those stops stay off this page until a photograph is of that stop. The ridge above Phia Den is the second frame of the park.

cards.title: Moss forest
cards.summary: The climb into moss and elfin forest. The park is 11,960 ha, set on 8 January 2014. The fee is check on arrival.

cards.title: The ridge
cards.summary: Karst above Phia Den on the western road. The summit named for the park is 1,935 m. Minutes from the city are check on arrival.

faqs.q: How long is the bus from Hanoi?
faqs.a: Vietnam Tourism says about 280 km and about eight hours. redBus prints about 282 km, with operator times from 4 hours 30 minutes to 8 hours 7 minutes and a listed average of 5 hours 49 minutes. Easybook quotes about 240 km and 6 to 7 hours. The road time is check on arrival.

faqs.q: When should you go to Ban Gioc?
faqs.a: From the end of November to the beginning of April the management board says the water is very low and asks you to come between 10:30 and 15:30. June to September is the fuller water, with heat and rain. A dry-season dam release is described between 10:30 and 13:00.

faqs.q: Can you see Pac Bo and the falls in one day?
faqs.a: Do not plan them as one afternoon. Pac Bo is about 55 km north on provincial road 203. Ban Gioc is more than 80 km east. Give each road its own day, and sleep in Dam Thuy if the falls are the morning.

season.label: Roads Oct–Apr; falls Jun–Sep
season.note: Vietnam Tourism calls October to April the drier travel season, November to February cold, and May to September rainy, hot, and humid. The falls are separate: the management board says the water is very low from the end of November to the beginning of April and asks visitors to come between 10:30 and 15:30. Fuller water is June to September. Mountain roads in storms are check on arrival.
